course_title: Professional Responsibilities, Ethical and Legal Issues in Computing
description: This course explores the professional, ethical, and legal responsibilities of computing professionals, focusing on cybersecurity standards such as ISO 27001 and NIST SP 800-53; ethical frameworks like the ACM Code of Ethics and IEEE Global Initiative on Ethics of Autonomous Systems; legal issues including data protection regulations such as GDPR and Jordan's Data Protection Law; and professional conduct in AI development using techniques like bias mitigation algorithms and explainable AI (XAI). It also covers the ethical implications of emerging technologies such as blockchain, IoT, and AI, including their impact on privacy, security, and digital rights.

clos.text: Define the core principles of the ACM Code of Ethics and their application to software development practices.
Describe the legal frameworks governing data protection, including GDPR, Jordan's Data Protection Law, and the EU-US Privacy Shield.
Explain the ethical challenges posed by AI technologies, including algorithmic bias and the use of explainable AI (XAI) techniques.
Apply ethical analysis frameworks to evaluate the impact of cybersecurity practices on user privacy and digital rights.
Implement best practices for professional conduct in the development and deployment of IoT systems, including secure data handling and transparency protocols.

topics: Introduction to professional responsibilities in computing
Privacy regulations: GDPR, Jordan's Data Protection Law
Ethics of AI and machine learning
Bias mitigation algorithms in AI systems
Explainable AI (XAI) techniques and their ethical implications
Ethical considerations in IoT system design
Professional conduct in software engineering projects
Digital rights management and content ownership
Ethical challenges in cloud computing and data storage
Case studies in ethical computing failures and successes
Emerging technologies and their ethical implications
Final review and professional ethics in practice
